_note: PLACEHOLDER army movement tuning. Every number here is a tunable placeholder, not approved balance. Confirmed (constitution): campaign movement uses a per-turn movement allowance in the Total War style; an army may move several times while its allowance permits. Costs: one movement point per meter of open ground, times the terrain cost of the cell entered (diagonal steps cost their real length). core/movement.gd applies these values; the terrain grid itself is data/movement_grid.json.

army._note: Movement points per turn, refilled on End Turn. The map is about 280 m across; Greyhaven to Crownwatch is about 75 m by road.

terrain._note: cost multiplies the distance walked into a cell of that terrain; null = impassable. Mountains are impassable except where a pass crosses them; water is impassable (no naval movement in this block).

roads._note: PLACEHOLDER RULE, not in the constitution: the constitution only confirms that road upgrades change the visible road surface. Here a road cell costs multiplier_by_level[road level] regardless of the terrain under it (dirt 0, gravel 1, stone 2). The road network is also what the map draws (main.gd reads it).

passes._note: Corridors through the mountains that stay passable (terrain 'pass'). Baked into the grid by main.gd --bake-movement-grid.

settlements._note: An army entering this radius around a settlement position (data/provinces.json) is at that settlement: its own settlement garrisons it; a foreign one would mean battle, which is not implemented.

armies._note: Destinations within this radius of another faction's army would mean battle (not implemented), so they are blocked.

grid_bake._note: Thresholds used only by the grid bake (main.gd --bake-movement-grid) to classify the map's terrain into data/movement_grid.json. Gameplay reads the baked grid, never the terrain mesh.
